events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a rider-filed safety dispute, so no automatic ruling is available and the case goes to a person: the trace marks SAFE-1 satisfied, meaning the judge writes a factual summary for the reviewer rather than deciding an amount [F4][SAFE-1].

What the record shows: at 17:09, one minute into the trip, the rider sent "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; one minute later the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat record contains only these two messages, both timestamped, so the exchange is complete [F5]. The driver, writing after the trip and outside the chat, says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and he told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on [F6].

What is disputed: whether the driver's words and conduct amounted to intimidation or threat of confinement, and whether the rider was in fact prevented from leaving. The driver frames it as a safety instruction [F6]; the rider frames it as a threat [F3][F4]. Reading the messages in context, an instruction coupled with "or I lock the doors" addressed to a rider asking to be let out is hostile language aimed at the other party and is at least abuse under Ryde's code of conduct, which bars abuse of any kind — so I record the safety screen as suspected and leave the characterisation to the human reviewer [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

I do not treat the ride itself as dangerous driving or as route misconduct: the actual path was 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km, i.e. no detour, and the duration ran 1.9 minutes over estimate, so no RD-1 obligation issue arises [F1][F2][RD-1].

Both briefs in this ablation requested no_action, but neither advocate was available and neither brief engages the SAFE-1 screen or the door/lock exchange at all; a no_action outcome would leave the chat exchange unexamined, so those requests cannot be adopted here [F4][F6][SAFE-1]. Nothing in the profile facts can decide the safety question: the rider's 619-day history, 4.8 rating and clean dispute record, and the driver's 893-day history, 4.62 rating, 1038 trips and zero upheld disputes are contextual only [F7][F8][RD-6].

Because the dispute type is safety and the screen is suspected, no amount is computed and no account flag is set here; the reviewer should specifically check the two chat messages and their timestamps [F3][F4][F5], the driver's post-trip assertion [F6], and whether the rider did or did not leave the vehicle at that point, which the fact table does not settle [F3][F6].
